title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; historical 1/7 of week lost, average 14.3% reduction in weekly sales

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: No past promotion lift at this price; noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is x1.0; price elasticity implies ~5% demand drop

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 3.2. Store closure on Monday (1/7 of week) reduces expected sales. Historical data shows no promotion lift at this price (5.72), and past promotions show noise-adjusted x1.0 effect. The week after a promotion typically sees x0.84, but no recent promotion. Price increase of 3.4% likely suppresses demand. No holiday or event. The classical model suggests no lift, consistent with noise-adjusted evidence. Adjust down for closure and price, but shrink toward 1.0 due to weak evidence. Downside spread increases slightly.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 9.9 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
